//: The two browser tests beside the app: `desk.test.ts` and
`studio.test.ts`, which serve `aab/` on a spare port and drive
the BUILT bundle in Chromium.
They are outside `tsconfig.json` because that one is the
BUILD: `npm run build` runs `tsc -b` over it before Vite, and
its `include` is `src`. A test in it would hold the desk's own
build to Playwright being installed, which is the mistake
`next/tsconfig.test.json` was split out for after it failed a
deploy.
So nothing typechecks these on their own, which is the trap
`scripts/check-types.ts` was written for: node strips the
annotations without reading them, so a `.ts` nobody checks is a
`.js` wearing them. That check runs this config too, and skips
it out loud where `app/node_modules` is absent, because
Playwright's types are the whole reason this config needs one.
`types` REPLACES rather than merges, so this names node's and
not React's: nothing here renders a component. Playwright is
not in that list either and does not belong there; it is
imported by name and its types come with the import.
NO `paths` here, on purpose. It replaces rather than merges
too, so an entry added here would lose the seven in the parent
that map `/content.js` and its neighbours on to the modules
the browser fetches. Nothing in these two files imports one:
what they drive is the built bundle over HTTP.
